title: A 3-factor from a minimum-degree bound
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on $n$ vertices, and suppose that $n$ is even and that the minimum degree $\delta$ of $G$ satisfies $n + 2 \le 2\delta$, that is, $\delta \ge \tfrac{n}{2} + 1$. Then $G$ has a $3$-factor: a spanning subgraph in which every vertex has degree exactly $3$.
hypotheses_covered: number of vertices n is even
minimum degree satisfies n + 2 ≤ 2δ (equivalently δ ≥ n/2 + 1)
